text:
maria: Heads up — hit a weird auth regession with the python SDK when spinning up two clients in the same process and rotating keys.
ajay: ugh, can you repro? what exactly is happening?
maria: repro is simple. Start two clients with different API keys set in env, then rotate one key at runtime. Client A keeps using old key even after os.environ updated.
sophie: is this sync or async client?
maria: async. using AsyncClient(...) wrapper from redwood.sdk with default providers.
taylor: can you paste minimal snippet? maybe env read happens at import time.
maria: sure — this is pared down:

```
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'key-A'
client_a = AsyncRedwoodClient()
# later
os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'] = 'key-B'
# new requests still authenticated as key-A
await client_a.generate(...)
```

ajay: that looks like provider caches the value on first init. expected if provider reads env once. but two clients with different keys in same process should be supported.
sophie: did you pass a key param directly to constructor or rely on env? if you pass, it should be per-client.
maria: relying on env in this test because our rotation mechanism swaps env for a subprocess that manages creds. we also tried calling client.refresh_credentials() and it still used old key.
taylor: hmm. sounds like credential resolution is global in runtime. iirc the library has a global CredentialProvider singleton.
ajay: if so, that's probably the cause. quick fix for you: create explicit per-client ApiKeyProvider that reads os.environ on each request or uses a callback.
maria: created a tiny workaround class that calls os.getenv inside get_auth_header every time and that fixed it. but this shouldn't be required.
sophie: agree. we should either document the behavior (provider caches) or change default to read per-call for env-backed keys. both have tradeoffs: perf vs dynamic rotation.
ajay: also might be an async-init race: if two clients init concurrently with different env values, the singleton could capture whichever initializes first.
taylor: can someone open an issue with repro and sample? include async repro and sync note.
maria: opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/842 with snippet and timing notes.
ajay: labeling: bug, auth, async, regression.
sophie: feature ask: add an AuthProvider interface that supports ephemeral callbacks and explicit refresh hooks + typed signatures for mypy users.
taylor: SDK owners: @dev-ops-bot can you route to eng-sdks and eng-ml? :eyes:
dev-ops-bot: Routing to #eng-sdks, #eng-ml (ticket: SDK-842)
ajay: small proposed API change: AsyncRedwoodClient(auth_provider=Callable[[],str]) — so callers can pass lambda that reads key each request.
sophie: that would help. also add docs section "env var rotation and multiple clients" with examples using per-client providers and a recipe for long-running processes.
maria: one more oddity — our test showed client_b created after rotation sometimes pick up key-B correctly, so behavior inconsistent depending on timing.
ajay: yep that's consistent with singleton capture or caching layer. reproducible with sleep between inits.
taylor: priority: medium-high. impact: customers running sidecars or credential refreshers.
sophie: followups: (1) add integration test that spawns two clients with different envs in same process and verifies auth headers; (2) add a small perf test to measure per-call env read vs cached.
ajay: i'll draft PR to make env-backed default provider optionally non-caching via flag env_read_strategy="per_call" | "cached".
maria: great. until then i'll keep the workaround provider in our codebase. TY for quick triage :thumbsup:
ajay: np. cc @taylor for docs snippets.
taylor: will add a short note in SDK-auth.md and snippet for async rotation pattern.
maria: thanks all — saving my debug notes here in case others hit it. :seedling:
